title: Use one shared conversational lead-in normalizer for chat and preflight
goal: Eliminate duplicated English and Vietnamese polite-prefix lists so chat input extraction and deterministic preflight cannot drift.
context: PR #528 aligned preflight behavior with SkillRuntime, but both stages still maintain separate lists and stripping loops. A future change could reintroduce mismatches. A shared deterministic helper should normalize only known lead-ins and must not change authorization, command grammar, or ordinary chat payloads.
forbidden_changes: Do not weaken workspace-only path restrictions, policy or approval checks, protected-path checks, size limits, cancellation, or read-back verification.
Do not convert arbitrary free-form chat into an executable command.
Do not treat provider prose as proof of tool execution.
Do not modify release workflows or claim physical-device acceptance without testing a real iPhone.
acceptance_criteria: SkillRuntime exposes one deterministic helper for stripping only supported conversational lead-ins.
Chat input extraction and preflight both use the same helper instead of maintaining duplicate prefix lists.
Ordinary chat and colon-delimited payload behavior remain unchanged.
Existing unsafe-path and incomplete-command tests remain intact.
Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA checks pass.
verification: Inspect Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA workflow results.
Physical iPhone acceptance remains tracked separately under Issue #347.
recovery: If shared normalization changes ordinary chat payloads, restore the original payload fallback and restrict normalization to preflight classification and supported actionable command extraction.
